# BlendPDF

> Free online PDF tools with no sign-up, no watermark, and no fees. Files are deleted from our servers within 1 hour — most immediately after processing. Full Arabic and RTL support (a rarity among PDF tools). Limits: up to 20 files per merge, 50 MB per file. Available in English, Spanish (https://blendpdf.com/es), French (https://blendpdf.com/fr) and Arabic (https://blendpdf.com/ar).

BlendPDF runs each tool as a dedicated page. Upload a file, process it, and download the result — no account is ever required.

## Organize

- [Merge PDF](https://blendpdf.com/merge-pdf): Combine up to 20 PDFs (50 MB each) into one file. Preserves text, links, forms, and RTL content. Free, no watermark.
- [Split PDF](https://blendpdf.com/split-pdf): Extract page ranges into one combined PDF, or split into separate files delivered as a ZIP.
- [Rotate PDF](https://blendpdf.com/rotate-pdf): Rotate individual pages or the whole document, with live previews.
- [Reorder Pages](https://blendpdf.com/reorder-pdf): Drag-and-drop page reordering with live thumbnails.
- [Delete Pages](https://blendpdf.com/delete-pages): Remove selected pages from a PDF.
- [Extract Pages](https://blendpdf.com/extract-pages): Pull selected pages into a new PDF (single file or one file per page as ZIP). Runs entirely in your browser.
- [Images to PDF](https://blendpdf.com/images-to-pdf): Convert JPG, PNG, and WebP images into a single PDF (A4 or fit-to-image pages).

## Convert

- [PDF to Word](https://blendpdf.com/pdf-to-word): Convert PDFs to editable .docx preserving layout, tables, and images (pdf2docx engine). Up to 500 pages.
- [PDF to Excel](https://blendpdf.com/pdf-to-excel): Extract tables from digital PDFs into .xlsx spreadsheets (one sheet per table).
- [Word to PDF](https://blendpdf.com/word-to-pdf): Convert .doc/.docx/.odt/.rtf documents to PDF via LibreOffice.
- [PowerPoint to PDF](https://blendpdf.com/powerpoint-to-pdf): Convert .ppt/.pptx/.odp presentations to PDF via LibreOffice.
- [Excel to PDF](https://blendpdf.com/excel-to-pdf): Convert .xls/.xlsx/.ods/.csv spreadsheets to PDF via LibreOffice.
- [PDF to Text](https://blendpdf.com/pdf-to-text): Extract the text layer of a PDF to a .txt file. Runs entirely in your browser — the file is never uploaded.
- [PDF to Images](https://blendpdf.com/pdf-to-images): Export PDF pages as high-resolution JPG images (ZIP download).
- [Extract Images](https://blendpdf.com/extract-images): Pull the embedded images out of a PDF as PNG files (ZIP download). Runs entirely in your browser.
- [PDF to PDF/A](https://blendpdf.com/pdf-to-pdfa): Convert a PDF to PDF/A-1b, 2b or 3b for archiving or a thesis deposit (Ghostscript via OCRmyPDF, no OCR). Every file is checked with veraPDF and the verdict is shown before download; a failed rule is named, never hidden. Up to 50MB.

## Optimize & Repair

- [Compress PDF](https://blendpdf.com/compress-pdf): Reduce PDF file size while keeping text selectable (Ghostscript-based). Returns the original if the file is already optimized.
- [Compress PDF to a size](https://blendpdf.com/compress-pdf/to-1mb): The compress tool opened with "Under a size limit" already set, for upload forms that refuse big files: [100 KB](https://blendpdf.com/compress-pdf/to-100kb), [200 KB](https://blendpdf.com/compress-pdf/to-200kb), [500 KB](https://blendpdf.com/compress-pdf/to-500kb), [1 MB](https://blendpdf.com/compress-pdf/to-1mb), [2 MB](https://blendpdf.com/compress-pdf/to-2mb). Tries the sharpest setting first and stops at the first one that fits; a colour phone scan of an A4 page is about 90 KB at good quality.
- [Compress PDF for a site's upload limit](https://blendpdf.com/fr/compress-pdf/for-ants): The same, preset to one site's documented limit, with its rules and source: [ANTS carte grise, 1 Mo](https://blendpdf.com/fr/compress-pdf/for-ants), [IRCC, 4 MB](https://blendpdf.com/compress-pdf/for-ircc), [Études en France, 10 Mo](https://blendpdf.com/fr/compress-pdf/for-campus-france), [ANEF, 10 Mo, 3 files per section](https://blendpdf.com/fr/compress-pdf/for-anef), [CAF, 10 Mo per send](https://blendpdf.com/fr/compress-pdf/for-caf), [France Travail, 5 Mo](https://blendpdf.com/fr/compress-pdf/for-france-travail).
- [PDF upload limits by portal](https://blendpdf.com/pdf-upload-limits): The largest PDF that government, visa and university portals accept (ANTS, CAF, ANEF, IRCC, USCIS, UCAS, IND and more), each with the portal's own words, a link to the source and the date it was checked. Free to reuse under CC BY 4.0, also as [CSV](https://blendpdf.com/pdf-upload-limits.csv) and [JSON](https://blendpdf.com/pdf-upload-limits.json). In English, French (/fr/...) and Arabic (/ar/...).
- [OCR PDF](https://blendpdf.com/ocr-pdf): Make scanned PDFs searchable with OCR — first-class Arabic support (plus English, French and Spanish). Up to 50 pages.
- [Repair PDF](https://blendpdf.com/repair-pdf): Attempt recovery of corrupted PDF files. Not all corruption is fixable — the tool is honest about failures.

## Security

- [Protect PDF](https://blendpdf.com/protect-pdf): Password-protect a PDF with AES-256 encryption.
- [Unlock PDF](https://blendpdf.com/unlock-pdf): Remove a password from a PDF you own (password required).
- [Remove Metadata](https://blendpdf.com/remove-metadata): Strip hidden metadata (author, software traces, timestamps) from a PDF before sharing. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [Add Watermark](https://blendpdf.com/watermark-pdf): Stamp text or image watermarks on every page.
- [Watermark a copy of your ID](https://blendpdf.com/watermark-pdf/id-copy): Type who the copy is for and what for; the watermark mode opens with that text and the date tiled across every page of the ID card or passport scan. Added in the browser: the file isn't uploaded unless the visitor emails it to themselves.

## Edit & Sign

- [Edit PDF](https://blendpdf.com/edit-pdf): Add text in Arabic or English (saved as real, selectable text), images, signatures, drawings, highlights and cover boxes, and rotate, reorder, delete or add pages. Runs entirely in your browser. Edit text (beta) changes existing text one line at a time: when you save, the old line's text is taken out of the page (not just covered) and the new text is written in its place, and if that can't be checked, nothing is saved. Scanned pages and some pages with shadow or transparency effects can't be changed this way, and it is not a full text editor.
- [Sign PDF](https://blendpdf.com/sign-pdf): Add a typed or image signature overlay to a PDF (visual signature, not a cryptographic one).
- [Add Page Numbers](https://blendpdf.com/add-page-numbers): Stamp customizable page numbers.
- [Crop PDF](https://blendpdf.com/crop-pdf): Trim margins or crop pages by dragging a rectangle on a live preview. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [Flatten PDF](https://blendpdf.com/flatten-pdf): Make filled form fields permanent and non-editable. Runs entirely in your browser.
- [Batch Fill Forms](https://blendpdf.com/fill-form): Fill any interactive PDF form, or batch-fill up to 50 copies from an Excel/CSV file with visual field mapping.
- [Form Templates](https://blendpdf.com/forms): Free fillable business form templates (W-9, NDA, I-9, lease agreement, patient intake) filled entirely in your browser.
- [Bilingual Arabic/English Templates](https://blendpdf.com/forms): Bilingual NDA, employment contract, and residential lease with English and Arabic side by side — Arabic input renders correctly in the PDF, filled entirely in your browser.

## Comparisons

Each was checked on 12 November 2026 without an account: what the saved files showed (renders where we have them) and the other service's own words. All are in English, French (/fr/...) and Arabic (/ar/...). Hub: [BlendPDF vs other editors](https://blendpdf.com/compare).

- [BlendPDF vs iLovePDF](https://blendpdf.com/blendpdf-vs-ilovepdf): iLovePDF's Edit PDF page says its Content Editor "does not currently support Right-to-Left (RTL) languages"; BlendPDF's Edit existing text (beta) changes an Arabic line right to left. iLovePDF takes bigger free files in some tools.
- [BlendPDF vs Smallpdf](https://blendpdf.com/blendpdf-vs-smallpdf): Smallpdf's free Add text saved two of three Arabic words, with unjoined letters; its existing-text editing is Pro only ("Direct PDF text editing requires a Pro subscription").
- [BlendPDF vs Sejda](https://blendpdf.com/blendpdf-vs-sejda): Sejda's editor warns that right-to-left and complex scripts aren't fully supported; its saved Arabic line ran off the page.
- [BlendPDF vs PDF24](https://blendpdf.com/blendpdf-vs-pdf24): PDF24 is free with no account or watermark, like BlendPDF, but saved an added Arabic line as a picture (not searchable) and doesn't edit existing text.
- [BlendPDF vs PDF Candy](https://blendpdf.com/blendpdf-vs-pdfcandy): PDF Candy's added Arabic was real text with joined letters, but its words came out in reverse order; its free plan has hourly limits.
- [BlendPDF vs Adobe Acrobat](https://blendpdf.com/blendpdf-vs-adobe-acrobat): from Adobe's own pages (not tested hands-on): its free online editor doesn't edit existing text and needs a free account to download.
- [BlendPDF vs PdfBayt](https://blendpdf.com/ar/blendpdf-vs-pdfbayt): the Arabic-only PdfBayt saved an added Arabic line as a picture, says its Add text doesn't change the original text, and needs an account for Compress and PDF to Word.

## Limits and policies

- Free with no account, no email requirement, and no watermarks on output.
- Maximum file size: 50 MB per file; merge accepts up to 20 files (100 MB total).
- Uploaded files are deleted from our servers within 1 hour; most are deleted immediately after processing. Form-template filling happens entirely in your browser — that data never reaches our servers.
- Privacy policy: https://blendpdf.com/privacy · Terms: https://blendpdf.com/terms

# Tool details and FAQs

## Add Page Numbers to PDF Online

Q: How does adding page numbers work?
A: We add page numbers to each page of your PDF at the position you choose. The numbers are embedded directly into the PDF, so they'll always be visible when the file is opened.

Q: Where can I place page numbers?
A: You can place page numbers at the top or bottom of pages, and align them to the left, center, or right. Choose the position that works best for your document.

Q: What page number formats are available?
A: You can choose from simple numbers (1, 2, 3), numbers with total (1 / 10), 'Page 1' format, or 'Page 1 of 10' format.

Q: Can I start numbering from a different number?
A: Yes! You can set the starting page number. For example, if you want to start from page 5, set 'Start From' to 5, and the first page will be numbered as 5.

Q: How do I add page numbers to a PDF online?
A: Upload your PDF (up to 50MB), pick one of six positions, choose a number format, set the starting number and font size, then click Add Page Numbers and download the numbered copy. The live preview shows the placement before you commit. No account or email is required.

Q: Can I skip the cover page or number only some pages?
A: Not directly — numbers are applied to every page. Workaround: use the Split PDF tool to separate the cover from the body, add numbers to the body (starting at whatever value you need), then merge the parts back together with the Merge PDF tool.

Q: What if my PDF already has page numbers?
A: The tool does not detect or remove existing numbering — it draws new numbers on top. If your document already has numbers at bottom-center, either place the new ones in a different position, such as a top corner, or remove the old numbering at the source and re-export before numbering.

Q: Can I use Arabic-Indic numerals or Arabic text in page numbers?
A: Not yet. Page numbers currently use Western digits (1, 2, 3) and English labels ("Page") in Latin script only. Arabic text support is coming. PDFs whose content is in Arabic number fine — the limitation applies only to the added label, not to your document.

Q: Is it safe to upload my document?
A: Yes. Files travel over an encrypted HTTPS connection and are deleted from our servers within one hour, most immediately after processing. We never read, store, or share document contents, and no account is needed. We only measure usage as anonymous totals, through Google Analytics and our own count of tool runs, never your documents.

Q: Can I add page numbers to a password-protected PDF?
A: No. The tool detects encrypted PDFs and returns a clear error. Remove the password first with the Unlock PDF tool (you need to know the password), add the numbers, then re-protect the file with the Protect PDF tool if needed.

Q: Does it work on scanned PDFs?
A: Yes. The number is drawn on top of each page, and a scanned page is just an image, so numbering works exactly as it does for regular PDFs. No OCR is involved or needed for numbering. If you also want the scanned text itself to become searchable, run the file through the BlendPDF OCR tool.

Q: What are the file size limits?
A: One PDF per operation, up to 50MB, and up to 20 files per 15 minutes per user. There is no page-count limit. If your file is over 50MB, compress it first with the Compress PDF tool.

Q: How does this compare to adding page numbers in Word or Adobe Acrobat?
A: Word numbers documents it edits, but converting an existing PDF into Word often breaks the layout. Acrobat Pro has a flexible header/footer tool but requires a paid subscription. BlendPDF numbers any existing PDF without altering its layout, free, in the browser, with no account.

Q: What should I do if I get an error?
A: Check that the file is a valid PDF under 50MB and not password-protected (unlock it first if it is). A "too many requests" message means you hit the 20-files-per-15-minutes limit — wait a few minutes. If a valid file still fails, it may be corrupted; run it through the Repair PDF tool first.

## Compress PDF Files Online

Q: How much can I compress a PDF?
A: Typically 50-90% reduction depending on the quality level you choose.

Q: Will compression affect text readability?
A: No. Text remains perfectly readable. Only images are compressed.

Q: How to compress PDF files online
A: Upload your PDF file, choose a compression level (Low, Medium, or High quality), and click "Compress PDF". The process takes 5-15 seconds and your compressed file will download automatically. Files are automatically deleted within one hour, most immediately after processing.

Q: What are the different compression levels?
A: BlendPDF offers three levels: Low Quality (80-90% reduction, ideal for screen viewing), Medium Quality (60-70% reduction, balanced for most uses), and High Quality (40-50% reduction, maintains near-original quality for printing).

Q: Will compression reduce PDF quality?
A: Text quality is never reduced as it uses lossless compression. Image quality depends on the compression level chosen. Low quality compresses images more aggressively, while high quality maintains image clarity.

Q: How much can I reduce PDF file size?
A: File size reduction depends on content and compression level. Typical reductions are: Low Quality 80-90%, Medium Quality 60-70%, High Quality 40-50%. Documents with many images see the greatest reduction.

Q: How are images compressed in PDFs?
A: Images are compressed using lossy compression algorithms that reduce file size while maintaining acceptable quality. The compression level determines how aggressively images are compressed. Higher quality levels preserve more image detail.

Q: Does compression work with Arabic PDFs?
A: Yes, BlendPDF works perfectly with Arabic PDFs and all RTL languages. Text quality is preserved, and formatting, character order, and text direction are maintained exactly as in the original document.

Q: What are the file size limits?
A: You can upload PDF files up to 50MB in size. There's no limit on the compressed file size you can download. Very large documents may take longer to process.

Q: How long does compression take?
A: Compression typically takes 5-15 seconds for most files. Larger files with many images may take 20-30 seconds. Processing speed depends on file size, page count, and compression level selected.

Q: Is my original file modified?
A: No, your original file is never modified. BlendPDF creates a new compressed version while leaving your original file completely untouched on your device. You can keep both versions.

Q: Can I compress password-protected PDFs?
A: Currently, password-protected PDFs cannot be compressed. You'll need to unlock the PDF first using an unlock tool, then compress it. Support for protected PDFs may be added in future updates.

Q: Can I compress PDFs on mobile devices?
A: Yes, BlendPDF works seamlessly on smartphones and tablets. The interface is mobile-optimized with touch-friendly controls. Compression speed is the same as on desktop since processing happens on our servers.

Q: Is PDF compression free?
A: Yes, compressing PDFs with BlendPDF is completely free — no fees, no watermarks, and no premium tiers today. All compression levels and features are available at no charge.

Q: What happens to my files after compression?
A: All uploaded files are automatically deleted from our servers within one hour, most immediately after processing. We never read, store, or share the contents of your documents. No permanent storage is maintained.

Q: What if compression fails or produces errors?
A: Common issues include file size limits (max 50MB), corrupted PDFs, or network problems. Try refreshing and retrying. If problems persist, verify your file opens correctly in a PDF viewer and check your internet connection.

## Crop PDF Pages Online

Q: Does cropping remove content or reduce the file size?
A: No. Cropping hides, not deletes — it sets the page's crop box, so content outside the selection is hidden from view but still stored in the file. That's also why cropping doesn't reduce the file size. If you need a smaller file, try our Compress PDF tool.

Q: Can I undo a crop?
A: Yes. Because cropping only hides content instead of deleting it, the crop is reversible — the hidden content can be restored later by resetting the crop box (for example by cropping again with a larger area, or with any PDF editor). Your original file also stays untouched on your device.

Q: Can I crop all pages at once?
A: Yes! Choose "All pages" and the same crop area is applied to every page — ideal for trimming uniform margins across the whole document. You can also crop just the current page.

Q: What if my pages have different sizes?
A: When cropping all pages, the selection is applied as the same relative area on each page — for example, the middle 80% — so it scales correctly even when page sizes differ.

Q: Is my PDF uploaded to a server?
A: No. Cropping runs in your browser — your file is opened and cropped locally on your device. It's only uploaded if you pick an option that needs our server, like converting to Word, and then it's deleted within an hour. It's free and requires no sign-up.

Q: How to crop PDF pages online
A: Upload your PDF (up to 50MB), drag a rectangle on the page preview to select the area you want to keep, choose whether to apply the crop to all pages or just the current page, then click "Apply Crop & Download". Everything runs in your browser.

Q: Can I crop just one page?
A: Yes. Choose "Current page only" and the crop is applied solely to the page you're viewing. Use the page navigation arrows to move to the page you want before applying.

Q: Does cropping work with Arabic PDFs?
A: Yes. Cropping only adjusts the visible page area, so Arabic text, right-to-left layout, diacritics, and mixed-language content are preserved exactly as they are in the original document.

Q: What are the file size limits?
A: You can open PDF files up to 50MB. There's no limit on the number of pages. Since processing happens on your own device, very large files simply depend on your device's memory and speed.

Q: How fast is cropping?
A: Cropping is nearly instant because there's no upload or download wait — the crop box update happens locally on your device. Speed depends on your device and browser, not on server load, and even large documents typically finish in seconds.

Q: Is my original file modified?
A: No. The tool creates a new PDF (named "cropped-" plus your original filename) with the crop applied, while your original file remains completely untouched on your device.

Q: Can I crop password-protected PDFs?
A: No, encrypted PDFs can't be opened for cropping. If you have the password and permission, unlock the PDF first with an unlock tool, then crop the unlocked copy.

Q: Can I crop PDFs on mobile devices?
A: Yes. The crop interface is touch-friendly — you can drag the crop rectangle with your finger on smartphones and tablets, and processing happens right on your device.

Q: Is cropping PDFs free?
A: Yes, cropping PDFs with BlendPDF is completely free — no fees, no watermarks, no account required, and no premium tiers today. All features are available at no charge.

Q: What if cropping fails or produces errors?
A: Common causes are files over 50MB, corrupted PDFs, or password-protected files. Verify the file opens in a PDF viewer, check the size, unlock encrypted files first, and try refreshing the page and cropping again.

## Delete PDF Pages Online

Q: Can I delete all pages?
A: No, you must keep at least one page in the document. This prevents creating an empty PDF file.

Q: Will this affect the quality of remaining pages?
A: No, the remaining pages will be exactly as they were in the original PDF, with no quality loss.

Q: Can I undo the deletion?
A: Once you download the modified PDF, the deletion is permanent. Make sure to keep a backup of your original file if needed.

Q: Does it work with password-protected PDFs?
A: Yes, if you have the password, you can unlock the PDF first and then delete pages from it.

Q: How to delete PDF pages online
A: Upload your PDF file, click on page thumbnails to select pages you want to delete (selected pages show red overlay), review your selection, then click "Delete [X] Page(s)". The process takes 5-10 seconds and your new PDF will download automatically.

Q: How does visual page selection work?
A: After uploading, you see thumbnail previews of all pages. Click on thumbnails to mark pages for deletion - selected pages show a red border, red overlay, and checkmark. Click again to unmark. A selection counter shows how many pages will be deleted.

Q: Can I select multiple pages at once?
A: Yes, you can click on multiple thumbnails to select them individually, or use "Select All" to select all pages at once, then deselect the ones you want to keep. At least one page must remain in the document.

Q: Does deleting pages preserve PDF quality?
A: Yes, deleting pages preserves all PDF quality for the remaining pages including formatting, images, text, fonts, and interactive elements. The quality of remaining pages is unchanged.

Q: Does page deletion work with Arabic PDFs?
A: Yes, BlendPDF works perfectly with Arabic PDFs and all RTL languages. Text direction, character order, and formatting are all preserved correctly for remaining pages.

Q: What are the file size limits?
A: You can upload PDF files up to 50MB in size. There's no limit on the number of pages you can delete. Very large documents may take slightly longer to process.

Q: How long does page deletion take?
A: Page deletion typically takes 5-10 seconds, depending on the number of pages and file complexity. The process is fast and efficient, with your new PDF ready for download almost immediately.

Q: Is my original file modified?
A: No, your original file is never modified. BlendPDF creates a new PDF with selected pages removed while leaving your original file completely untouched on your device.

Q: Can I delete pages on mobile devices?
A: Yes, BlendPDF works seamlessly on smartphones and tablets. The visual page selection interface is touch-friendly and works perfectly on mobile devices.

Q: Is deleting PDF pages free?
A: Yes, deleting PDF pages with BlendPDF is completely free — no fees, no watermarks, and no premium tiers today. All features are available at no charge.

Q: What happens to my files after deletion?
A: All uploaded files are automatically deleted from our servers within one hour, most immediately after processing. We never read, store, or share the contents of your documents. No permanent storage is maintained.

Q: What if page deletion fails or produces errors?
A: Common issues include file size limits, corrupted PDFs, or network problems. Try refreshing and retrying. Verify your file opens correctly in a PDF viewer and check your internet connection.

## Edit PDF in Arabic or English

Q: Does Arabic text come out right?
A: Yes. Letters join, numbers and brackets stay in order, and Arabic and English can share a line. It is saved as real text, not a picture, so most of it can be selected and searched.

Q: Can I change text that is already in the PDF?
A: Yes, one line at a time, with Edit existing text (beta). Click a line, check or retype it, and when you save, the old words are taken out of the page, not just covered, and yours are written in their place. The line keeps its own font when that font has every letter you type. If it doesn't, we use the closest font we have and tell you. Scanned pages and some pages with shadows or see-through effects can't be changed this way, so use Hide (white box) there. It only hides what's underneath; it stays in the file.

Q: Is my PDF uploaded anywhere?
A: No. Everything happens in your browser and the file stays on your device. It only reaches our server if you pick an option that needs it, like converting to Word, or choose to get the result by email.

Q: What happens to fillable form fields?
A: When you save, the fields and what's typed in them become part of the page, so your additions sit on top. The saved PDF can't be filled in again.

Q: Is it free? Is there a watermark?
A: Yes, it's free, and that includes Edit existing text. There's no account to create and no watermark on your file, unless you add one yourself.

Q: Does it work on a phone?
A: Yes. It runs in the browser on phones and tablets, so there's nothing to install, and you can draw your signature with your finger.

Q: Can I edit a PDF that has a password?
A: Yes, if you know the password. Type it when you're asked and the PDF opens in the editor. If it only has restrictions that stop editing, you can remove them in one step.

## Excel to PDF - Free Converter

Q: What spreadsheet formats are supported?
A: We support Microsoft Excel (.xls, .xlsx), OpenDocument Spreadsheet (.ods), and CSV files. All sheets in your workbook are included in the PDF.

Q: How are wide spreadsheets handled?
A: The PDF follows your sheet's page setup, the same as printing from Excel. Sheets wider than a page are split across multiple PDF pages. For a tighter fit, set the print area or scaling in your spreadsheet before converting.

Q: What happens to formulas?
A: The PDF shows each cell's calculated value, not the formula behind it. Charts and cell formatting like colors, borders, and number formats are carried over.

Q: What are the file size limits?
A: You can convert spreadsheets up to 50MB in size. There's no limit on the number of sheets or rows, but larger files may take longer to process.

Q: Is my spreadsheet secure?
A: Yes. Your files are processed securely and never stored — Files are deleted from our servers within 1 hour — most immediately after processing. We never read or share your spreadsheets.

Q: Is this really free?
A: Yes, completely free! No sign-up, no credit card, no hidden fees. Convert as many Excel spreadsheets to PDF as you need.

Q: How to convert Excel to PDF online
A: Upload your spreadsheet (.xls, .xlsx, .ods, or .csv) by dragging it onto the upload area or clicking "Select File", then click the convert button. The conversion runs on our servers and your PDF downloads in seconds.

Q: Are all sheets in my workbook included?
A: Yes, all sheets in the workbook are included in the PDF. If you only want certain sheets, delete or hide the others in a copy of the file before converting, or split the resulting PDF afterwards.

Q: Is cell formatting preserved?

## Extract Images from PDF

Q: Why did I get no images, or just one big image per page?
A: This tool extracts pictures that are embedded in the PDF as image objects. Charts, logos, and diagrams are often vector graphics — drawn with lines and shapes, not stored as images — so there is nothing to extract. Scanned PDFs work the other way: each page is usually one big photo, so you'll get a single full-page image per page. If you want every page saved as a picture regardless, use our PDF to Images tool instead.

Q: What format do the extracted images come in?
A: All images are saved as PNG files, which is lossless — nothing is recompressed, so you keep the full quality that was stored in the PDF. Note that images originally embedded as JPEG are converted to PNG on the way out, so file sizes can be larger than the originals.

Q: Is my PDF uploaded to your servers?
A: No. Getting the images out runs in your browser — your PDF is opened and processed locally on your device, which is also why it's fast: there's no upload or download wait. It's only uploaded if you pick an option that needs our server, like converting to Word, and then it's deleted within an hour.

Q: Why do I see fewer images than the PDF appears to contain?
A: We automatically remove duplicates — a logo or header image that repeats on every page is extracted only once. We also skip tiny images under 16×16 pixels, which are usually invisible artifacts or masks rather than real pictures.

Q: How is this different from the PDF to Images tool?
A: PDF to Images renders each full page as one picture — text, graphics, and all. Extract Images pulls out only the original photos and pictures embedded inside the PDF, at their original stored resolution. Use this tool to recover the actual photos; use PDF to Images to get page snapshots.

Q: How to extract images from a PDF online
A: Open your PDF (up to 50MB) in the box above and click Get the pictures. BlendPDF scans every page and hands you a ZIP with each picture as a PNG file; if the PDF holds a single picture, you get that PNG on its own. Everything runs in your browser.

Q: Can I choose which images to download?
A: Not inside the tool: you get every picture in one ZIP. Each file is named with its number and its size in pixels, for example image_004_1600x1200.png, so the one you want is easy to spot. To get only the pictures from certain pages, keep those pages first with Extract Pages, then open the new file here.

Q: Are there page or image limits?
A: Files up to 50MB are accepted. To keep your browser responsive, scanning covers the first 200 pages and stops after 500 images — you'll see a clear notice if either cap is reached, and splitting the PDF lets you extract the rest.

Q: Is the image quality preserved?
A: Yes. Images are extracted at the exact resolution they're stored at inside the PDF and saved as lossless PNG — no scaling, no recompression. A 2000×1500 embedded photo comes out as a 2000×1500 PNG.

Q: Does it work with Arabic PDFs?
A: Yes. Image extraction reads embedded pictures, which are language-independent — Arabic and RTL documents are scanned exactly like any other PDF, and the fully localized Arabic interface is available too.

Q: How fast is image extraction?
A: The scan runs page by page with a live progress bar, typically finishing in seconds. Speed depends on your device and the document's size, not on server load — there's no upload or download wait.

Q: Can I extract images from password-protected PDFs?
A: No, encrypted PDFs are detected and rejected with a hint to unlock them first. If you have the password and permission, remove the protection with an unlock tool, then extract from the unlocked copy.

Q: Can I extract images on mobile devices?
A: Yes. Open the PDF on your phone or tablet, tap Get the pictures and the ZIP (or the single PNG) saves to your device. Most phones open ZIP files in their Files app. The work happens on the phone itself.

Q: Is extracting images free?
A: Yes, completely free — no fees, no watermarks, no account, and no premium tiers today. All features, including the ZIP download and selection controls, are included.

Q: What if extraction fails or produces errors?
A: Check that the file is a valid PDF under 50MB and not password-protected. If pages contain only vector graphics you'll get a "no images found" result rather than an error — try the PDF to Images tool instead. Refreshing and retrying resolves most one-off failures.

## Flatten PDF Online

Q: What does flattening a PDF mean?
A: Flattening merges interactive form fields — text boxes, checkboxes, dropdowns, radio buttons — into the page content itself. The answers stay visible, but the fields are gone, so nobody can edit them anymore.

Q: When should I flatten a PDF form?
A: Flatten after you've filled a form and before you submit, email, or print it. It locks your answers in place and ensures the form looks the same in every PDF viewer. You can fill forms first with our Fill Form tool, then flatten the result here.

Q: Can flattening be undone?
A: No — flattening is permanent in the output file. The original file on your device is never modified, though, so keep it if you may need to edit the form again later.

Q: Why does it say my PDF has no form fields?
A: Only PDFs with interactive (AcroForm) fields can be flattened. If your form is a scanned image or plain text with underscores, there is nothing interactive to lock — the document is already non-editable in that sense.

Q: Is my file uploaded to a server?
A: No. Flattening runs in your browser — the PDF is read, flattened, and saved on your own device. Your file only leaves your computer if you pick an option that needs our server, like converting to Word, and then it's deleted within an hour.

Q: Which form field types can be flattened?
A: All standard interactive (AcroForm) fields: text boxes, checkboxes, radio buttons, and dropdown lists. The tool lists every detected field by name before flattening, so you can see exactly what will be merged into the page.

Q: Can I fill a form before flattening it?
A: Yes — that's the intended workflow. Use the BlendPDF Fill Form tool to type your answers into the interactive fields, download the filled PDF, then flatten it here so the answers can't be changed.

Q: Can I flatten password-protected PDFs?
A: Not directly — encrypted PDFs can't be modified without the password. Remove the password first with the BlendPDF Unlock PDF tool, then flatten the unlocked file.

Q: What are the file size limits?
A: PDF files up to 50MB are supported, with no page limit. Since flattening runs locally in your browser, speed depends on your device rather than any server.

Q: Is my original file modified?
A: No. The flattened document is saved as a new file prefixed with "flattened-", and your original — with its editable fields — stays untouched on your device.

Q: Can I flatten PDFs on mobile devices?
A: Yes, the tool works on smartphones and tablets. You can review the detected field list, flatten, and download the locked copy directly from your mobile browser.

Q: Is flattening PDFs free?
A: Yes — completely free, with no sign-up, no watermarks, and no premium tiers today. Files up to 50MB are supported, and you can flatten as many forms as you need.

Q: Does flattening work with Arabic PDF forms?
A: Yes. Flattening merges each field's rendered appearance into the page, so Arabic answers and RTL layouts are preserved as displayed. BlendPDF is built Arabic-first, and the rest of the document's Arabic text is untouched by flattening.

Q: What if flattening fails or produces errors?
A: A small number of PDFs use exotic field appearance streams that the flattening engine can't process; in that case you get a clear error and your file is left unchanged. Password-protected files must be unlocked first, and corrupted files should be repaired or re-exported before retrying.

## OCR PDF — Make Scanned PDFs Searchable

Q: What is OCR and what does this tool do?
A: OCR (optical character recognition) turns pictures of text — like scanned pages or photographed documents — into real text a computer can read. This tool adds that recognized text as an invisible layer inside your PDF, so the file looks exactly the same but becomes searchable, selectable, and copyable.

Q: How good is the Arabic OCR?
A: Arabic is a first-class language here, not an afterthought — we use the Tesseract engine with its dedicated Arabic model, which handles connected script and right-to-left text properly. Accuracy is good but not perfect: it depends heavily on scan quality, so clean 300-DPI scans of printed text work far better than blurry photos or handwriting. For best results, scan straight, well-lit pages.

Q: What are the file limits?
A: Files can be up to 50MB and 50 pages. OCR is genuinely slow — expect roughly 1–2 seconds per page — so larger documents would time out. If your file is bigger, split it with our Split PDF tool and OCR the parts separately, or compress it first.

Q: Why does it say my PDF already has text?
A: If every page already contains a text layer (for example, a PDF exported from Word), there is nothing for OCR to add, so we tell you instead of silently returning the same file. If the existing text is wrong or garbled, enable "Re-OCR pages that already have text" to replace it with freshly recognized text.

Q: Is my document safe?
A: OCR runs on our server, since text recognition is too heavy to do in your browser. Your file is processed in temporary storage and automatically deleted within 1 hour — we never read, share, or keep your documents.

Q: Can I turn the scanned PDF into a Word document?
A: Yes — a great workflow is to OCR the scan here first, then run the searchable result through our PDF to Word tool. Without the OCR step, a scanned PDF converts to Word as images; with it, you get editable text.

Q: How to make a scanned PDF searchable
A: Upload your scanned PDF, tick the recognition languages it contains (Arabic, English, French, or Spanish), and click the OCR button. Processing takes roughly 1-2 seconds per page, then the searchable PDF downloads with an invisible text layer added over each scan.

Q: Which languages are supported?
A: Four languages are supported: Arabic, English, French, and Spanish. You can select any combination for mixed-language documents, such as Arabic contracts with English clauses. At least one language must be selected before running OCR.

Q: Does OCR change how my PDF looks?
A: No. The recognized text is placed as an invisible layer exactly on top of the original scan, so the document looks identical — stamps, signatures, and layout untouched — but becomes searchable and copyable.

Q: What are the file size and page limits?
A: Files can be up to 50MB and 50 pages. OCR is computationally heavy — roughly 1-2 seconds per page — so larger documents would time out. Split bigger files with the Split PDF tool and OCR the parts separately, or compress oversized files first.

Q: How long does OCR take?
A: Expect roughly 1-2 seconds per page, so a 30-page scan can take about a minute. OCR jobs run one at a time on the server; at busy moments you may be asked to retry in a minute.

Q: How accurate is the OCR?
A: Accuracy is good but never perfect, and depends heavily on scan quality. Clean, straight, well-lit 300-DPI scans of printed text give excellent results; blurry photos, skewed pages, and low-resolution scans reduce accuracy in any OCR system.

Q: Can OCR read handwriting?
A: Not reliably. The recognition engine is designed for printed, typeset text. Neat block capitals may partially recognize, but cursive handwriting — in any language — generally will not. Handwritten notes and signatures stay visible in the PDF; they just will not become searchable text.

Q: Can I OCR a password-protected PDF?
A: No, encrypted PDFs are rejected with a clear message. Remove the password first with the Unlock PDF tool, run OCR on the unlocked file, then re-protect the result if needed.

Q: Is OCR free?
A: Yes, completely free — no sign-up, no watermarks, and no premium tiers today. Because OCR is the heaviest tool on our servers, usage is limited to 5 documents per 15 minutes, which covers normal use comfortably.

Q: What happens to my files after OCR?
A: All uploaded files are automatically deleted from our servers within one hour, most immediately after processing. We never read, store, or share the contents of your documents. No permanent storage is maintained.

Q: What if OCR fails or produces errors?
A: The tool reports specific problems: files over 50MB or 50 pages, password-protected PDFs, pages that already have text, or a busy server. Each message says what to do — split, unlock, enable re-OCR, or retry in a minute.

## Convert PDF to Excel Online

Q: How does PDF to Excel conversion work?
A: We use advanced table detection algorithms to identify tables in your PDF, extract the data, and convert it to Excel format. Multiple tables are saved to separate sheets in the Excel file.

Q: What if my PDF doesn't have tables?
A: If your PDF doesn't contain extractable table data, the conversion will fail with an error message. This tool is specifically designed for PDFs that contain tabular data.

Q: What happens if my PDF has multiple tables?
A: If your PDF contains multiple tables, each table will be extracted and saved to a separate sheet in the Excel file. The sheets will be named 'Table_1', 'Table_2', etc.

Q: Will the formatting be preserved?
A: We extract the data and structure of tables. Basic formatting like cell alignment and borders may be preserved, but complex formatting may be simplified in the Excel output.

Q: How to convert PDF to Excel online
A: Upload your PDF by clicking "Choose file" or dragging it onto the upload area, click "Convert to Excel", and download the resulting XLSX file. The tool scans every page for tables, extracts the data, and builds a spreadsheet. No account or email is required.

Q: How does the table extraction work?
A: BlendPDF analyzes the text layer of your PDF to detect table structures on every page, then rebuilds the rows and columns as real spreadsheet cells. It extracts data and structure, not visual styling, so you get an editable spreadsheet rather than a picture of a table.

Q: Is the PDF to Excel converter free?
A: Yes. No watermark, no row or page limits designed to upsell you, no sign-up, and no subscription. The practical limits are technical: 50MB per file and about 20 conversions per 15 minutes.

Q: Is it safe to upload financial documents?
A: Files are uploaded over an encrypted connection, document contents are never read, stored, or shared, and files are deleted from our servers within one hour, most immediately after processing. No account is needed. We only measure usage as anonymous totals, through Google Analytics and our own count of tool runs, never your documents.

Q: Why do I get a "No tables found" error?
A: The tool needs an actual table structure in the PDF's text layer. You will see this error if the PDF is a scan with no text layer (run it through the BlendPDF OCR tool first), if the data is laid out as plain text rather than a table, or if the file contains only images of tables.

Q: Can I convert a scanned PDF to Excel?
A: Not directly. The converter reads the PDF's text layer, so tables that exist only as scanned images cannot be extracted. Run the PDF through the BlendPDF OCR tool first to add a text layer, then convert it here.

Q: Will formatting, colors, and formulas be preserved?
A: No, and no converter can preserve formulas, because PDFs only store the calculated values, never the formulas behind them. You get the data and table structure. Cell colors, borders, and fonts are not carried over; add formatting and formulas in Excel afterward.

Q: How accurate is the extraction?
A: Clean, grid-like tables extract very reliably. Tables with merged cells, multi-line headers, nested sub-tables, or values that span columns can come out misaligned and need a few minutes of cleanup. Always spot-check totals against the original PDF.

Q: What are the file size limits?
A: One PDF at a time, up to 50MB, with all pages scanned for tables. Processing is capped at about two minutes, so extremely long documents may time out; split them first and convert in parts.

Q: Can I convert password-protected PDFs?
A: Not directly. If you have the password and the right to use the document, remove the protection with the BlendPDF unlock tool first, then convert the unlocked file.

Q: Does it work with Arabic or RTL tables?
A: Partially, and we would rather be honest about it: right-to-left text is a hard case for table extraction. Arabic column order and text may need manual correction in Excel after conversion. Numeric data usually survives better than the text labels around it.

Q: Is this better than copying and pasting from the PDF?
A: For anything bigger than a few cells, yes. Copy-paste from a PDF typically collapses a table into one column or one long line, losing the structure. The converter preserves rows and columns and handles all pages at once.

Q: What should I check after converting?
A: Three quick checks: that numbers imported as numbers rather than text (look for left-aligned numerals), that no header rows slipped into the data, and that each expected table has its own sheet. Excel's "Convert to Number" and "Text to Columns" fix most import quirks in seconds.

Q: Should I choose JPG or PNG?
A: PNG is lossless and best for pages with text, line art, or diagrams, where crisp edges matter. JPG produces smaller files and works well for photo-heavy pages. If you are unsure, PNG for documents, JPG for photos.

Q: What resolution and quality do I get?
A: Pages are rendered at a true 300 DPI, meaning an A4 page becomes an image of roughly 2480 x 3508 pixels. That is print-quality resolution, and JPG output uses a high quality setting of 95 to keep compression artifacts minimal.

Q: Is the PDF to images converter free, without a watermark?
A: Yes. No watermark on any image, no per-page fees, no sign-up, and no paid tier. The technical limits are 50MB per file and 100 pages per conversion.

Q: Is it safe to convert my PDF online?
A: Files are uploaded over an encrypted connection, document contents are never read, stored, or shared, and files are deleted from our servers within one hour, most immediately after processing. No account is needed. We only measure usage as anonymous totals, through Google Analytics and our own count of tool runs, never your documents.

Q: How do I receive the images?
A: All pages arrive in a single ZIP file with zero-padded names like page-001.jpg so they sort in the correct order. You can also preview every page in the browser and download any single page individually without downloading the whole ZIP.

Q: Can I convert only specific pages?
A: Not directly; the tool converts every page. To convert a subset, first extract the pages you want using the BlendPDF split or delete-pages tool, then convert the smaller PDF. That also keeps the ZIP small.

Q: Does it work with Arabic and RTL PDFs?
A: Yes, very well. Rendering to an image is a faithful visual snapshot of each page, so Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, and Urdu text appears exactly as it does in the PDF, with no text reconstruction involved and nothing to reflow or misorder.

Q: Will scanned PDFs convert properly?
A: Yes. A scanned PDF is already images inside a PDF wrapper, so conversion simply exports each page. Output quality mirrors the original scan; rendering at 300 DPI cannot add detail that the scanner did not capture.

Q: Can I search or copy text from the images?
A: No. JPG and PNG files contain pixels only, with no text layer, so the images are not searchable and text cannot be selected. If you need editable text, use the BlendPDF PDF to Word tool on a text-based PDF; for scans, run the BlendPDF OCR tool first to add a text layer.

Q: Can I convert a password-protected PDF to images?
A: No. Encrypted PDFs cannot be rendered. If you have the password and the right to use the document, remove the protection with the BlendPDF unlock tool first, then convert.

Q: Why not just take screenshots?
A: Screenshots are capped at your screen resolution, typically 100-150 DPI of effective detail, and capturing a long document page by page is slow and error-prone. This tool renders every page at a true 300 DPI in one pass, with consistent sizing and correct ordering.

Q: What if the conversion fails or the ZIP is huge?
A: Check the file is a valid, unencrypted PDF under 50MB and 100 pages. For a smaller ZIP, choose JPG instead of PNG. Repeated failures on a damaged file can often be fixed by running it through the BlendPDF repair tool first. The rate limit is about 10 conversions per 15 minutes.

## PDF to PDF/A Converter

Q: What is PDF/A?
A: PDF/A is the version of PDF made for long-term archiving (ISO 19005). Everything needed to show the file is inside it: the fonts are embedded and the colours are defined, so it will look the same in twenty years on any computer. Universities, courts and public archives ask for it.

Q: Which PDF/A level should I choose?
A: The one your university or archive names. If they don't say, choose PDF/A-2b: it is the most widely accepted. PDF/A-1b is for older rules that ask for PDF/A-1 by name: it doesn't allow transparency, so pages that use it are saved as pictures, and we tell you which ones. PDF/A-3b is only for when you were asked for PDF/A-3. The "b" means the file looks exactly right. The "a" levels also need an accessible tag structure, which this tool doesn't make.

Q: How do I know the file really is PDF/A?
A: Every file is checked with veraPDF, the open-source validator from the PDF Association and the Open Preservation Foundation, which many universities use themselves. Its verdict is shown next to the download. If it finds a problem, we tell you which rule failed instead of calling the file valid.

Q: Can I use it for my thesis or dissertation?
A: Yes. Export your thesis to PDF from Word, LaTeX, Google Docs or Pages, upload it here and choose the level your graduate school asks for. Google Docs can't export PDF/A, and LaTeX needs extra packages for it, so this is the quickest route for many students.

Q: What changes in my file?
A: It looks the same. Fonts are embedded, colours are set to standard RGB and the archiving information is added. Fillable form fields become part of the page: what you typed stays, but it can't be edited anymore. A password can't be kept, because PDF/A doesn't allow encryption.

Q: Does it work with scanned PDFs?
A: Yes. The pages stay pictures, exactly as they were scanned. To make the text searchable too, run OCR PDF first, then convert the result to PDF/A.

Q: Can I convert a digitally signed PDF?
A: No. The conversion rewrites the file, which would break the signature. Convert the unsigned version, then sign the PDF/A.

Q: Does it keep Arabic and other right-to-left text?
A: Yes. Arabic text keeps its fonts and joined letters, and stays selectable and searchable in the PDF/A file.

Q: Is it free, and what happens to my file?
A: It's free, with no sign-up, for PDFs up to 50MB. The conversion runs on our server and the file is deleted within an hour.

## PDF to Text Converter

Q: Is my PDF uploaded to a server?
A: No. The text is extracted locally in your browser, which also makes it fast and private. Your file only leaves your device if you pick an option that needs our server, like converting to Word, and then it's deleted within an hour.

Q: Why is no text extracted from my scanned PDF?
A: Scanned PDFs are images of pages and have no text layer, so there is no text to extract. That requires OCR (optical character recognition) — use our OCR PDF tool to add a searchable text layer (Arabic, English, French, and Spanish supported), then extract the text here. This tool works with PDFs that contain real, selectable text.

Q: How do I copy text from a PDF?
A: Drop your PDF and click "Get the text". You get a .txt file with all the text, page by page, which you can open in any text editor and copy from. It all happens in your browser.

Q: Will the layout and formatting be preserved?
A: You get plain text: paragraphs and line breaks are kept as well as possible, but fonts, colors, columns and tables are not preserved. For editable formatting, try our PDF to Word tool.

Q: Is this PDF to text converter free?
A: Yes — completely free, with no sign-up and no watermarks. Files up to 50MB are supported, and since everything runs in your browser there is nothing to wait for on a server.

Q: How to extract text from a PDF online
A: Drop your PDF and click "Get the text". The text is read page by page, directly in your browser, and saved as a .txt file named after your PDF. Nothing is uploaded to a server unless you pick an option that needs our server, like converting to Word.

Q: Can I copy the text instead of downloading it?
A: Not straight to the clipboard. "Get the text" gives you a .txt file with the full text; open it in any text editor or notes app and copy what you need.

Q: Does it extract Arabic text?

Q: What are the page separators?

A: You can load PDF files up to 50MB. There is no page limit — a progress bar shows extraction advancing page by page. Because processing is local, large files depend on your device's speed rather than on any server.

Q: How long does text extraction take?
A: Most PDFs are done in a few seconds. Since everything runs in your browser, speed depends on your device and the document's size and complexity — there is no upload or download wait, and no server queue.

Q: Is my original file modified?
A: No. The tool only reads your PDF to extract its text; the file itself is never changed. The extracted text is saved as a separate .txt file, and your original PDF stays exactly as it was on your device.

Q: Can I extract text from password-protected PDFs?
A: Not directly. Encrypted PDFs cannot be opened without the password, so the tool will show a hint instead of a result. Remove the password first with the BlendPDF Unlock PDF tool, then extract the text.

Q: Can I extract text on mobile devices?
A: Yes, the tool works on smartphones and tablets. Extraction runs locally in your mobile browser, and you can copy the text to your clipboard or download the .txt file just like on desktop.

Q: What happens to my file after extraction?
A: Your PDF is read locally in your browser's memory and released when you close or reload the page, and the extracted text stays on your device. Nothing is uploaded unless you pick an option that needs our server, like converting to Word; a file sent there is deleted within an hour.

Q: What if extraction fails or the text looks wrong?
A: Common causes are scanned PDFs without a text layer (use the OCR tool), password protection (unlock first), corrupted files, or the 50MB limit. Odd word order or spacing usually reflects how text is stored inside the PDF. Refresh the page and try again if extraction fails unexpectedly.

Q: How accurate is the conversion?
A: BlendPDF uses the pdf2docx engine, which reconstructs paragraphs, tables, and images from text-based PDFs with good fidelity. Simple, single-column documents convert very well. Complex multi-column layouts, heavy graphic design, and right-to-left text may need manual cleanup after conversion.

A: Text, images, and most tables carry over. Fonts are matched as closely as possible, and paragraph structure is rebuilt so the document is genuinely editable. Elements that commonly shift are text boxes, footnotes, multi-column sections, and decorative layouts.

A: Not into editable text directly. The converter reads the PDF's text layer, so a scanned page is an image and no words can be extracted from it; the output would contain the page images rather than editable text. Run the file through the BlendPDF OCR tool first to add a text layer, then convert.

Q: Does it work with Arabic and other RTL PDFs?
A: You can convert them, but right-to-left text is one of the hardest cases for any PDF-to-Word engine, including ours. Expect the text to come through, with word order, joining, or alignment sometimes needing cleanup in Word. Simple Arabic documents fare much better than complex layouts.

Q: Can I convert a password-protected PDF?

A: You get a DOCX file, the standard Microsoft Word format. It opens in Word, Google Docs, LibreOffice, and Pages. If you need the older DOC format, open the DOCX in any of those apps and save it as DOC.

Q: How does BlendPDF compare to Word or Adobe Acrobat?
A: Microsoft Word can open PDFs directly and Adobe Acrobat Pro has a strong exporter, but Word's results vary and Acrobat requires a paid license. BlendPDF is free, works in the browser with no install, and handles text-based documents well. For extremely complex layouts, Acrobat Pro may still do better.

Q: Why does my converted file look different from the PDF?
A: The most common causes are fonts that were not embedded in the PDF (substituted fonts change line breaks), multi-column or designed layouts, and scanned pages, which convert as images unless you add a text layer with the BlendPDF OCR tool first. Small spacing differences are normal and quick to fix in Word.

Q: What if the conversion fails or I get an error?
A: Check that the file is a valid, unencrypted PDF under 50MB. If the PDF is damaged, run it through the BlendPDF repair tool first. A "too many requests" message means you hit the limit of about 10 conversions per 15 minutes; wait a few minutes and try again.

Q: How does PDF password protection work?

Q: What makes a strong password?
A: Use a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters. Avoid common words or personal information. The longer the password, the more secure it is.

Q: Can I remove the password later?

Q: What if I forget the password?
A: Unfortunately, if you forget the password, there's no way to recover it. The encryption is designed to be secure, so we cannot access your PDF without the password. Make sure to save your password in a secure place.

A: Upload your PDF (up to 50MB), type the password you want to use, and click "Protect PDF". BlendPDF encrypts the file with AES-256 and gives you a protected copy to download. No account or email is required.

Q: What encryption does BlendPDF use to protect PDFs?
A: BlendPDF encrypts your PDF with AES-256, the strongest encryption level defined in the PDF standard, using the qpdf engine. The password you set is required to open the file in any PDF viewer.

Q: Is it safe to protect a PDF online?
A: Yes. Uploads travel over an encrypted HTTPS connection, your password is used once to encrypt the file and is never stored, and files are deleted from our servers within one hour, most immediately after processing. We never read, store, or share document contents. We only collect aggregate, anonymous usage analytics.

Q: Is protecting a PDF free? Is there a watermark?
A: Yes, it is completely free. There is no watermark, no page limit, no daily quota that pushes you to a paid plan, and no premium tier. The protected file you download is your document, unchanged except for the encryption.

Q: Do I need an account or email address?
A: No. You can protect a PDF without creating an account or entering an email address. An optional email-delivery feature exists if you want the file sent to your inbox, but downloading directly never requires an email.

Q: Can I protect a PDF that already has a password?
A: No. If the PDF is already encrypted, the tool returns an error asking you to unlock it first. Use the Unlock PDF tool with the current password, then protect the unlocked file with your new password.

Q: Does this stop people from printing or copying my PDF?
A: Not separately. BlendPDF sets an open password: nobody can open the file without it. It does not currently offer print-only or copy-only restrictions, and anyone who knows the password can use the document normally once it is open.

A: One PDF per operation, up to 50MB. If your file is larger, run it through the Compress PDF tool first and then protect the compressed copy.

Q: Will protecting the PDF change its content or quality?
A: No. Encryption wraps the existing content without re-rendering it. Text, images, fonts, links, and layout are unchanged, and the file size stays roughly the same.

Q: Can a password-protected PDF be opened on any device?
A: Any reasonably modern PDF viewer can open AES-256 protected files, including Adobe Acrobat Reader, macOS Preview, Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and the standard iOS and Android viewers. Only very old software from before roughly 2010 may fail to open AES-256 files.

Q: How does BlendPDF compare to protecting a PDF in Adobe Acrobat or Word?

Adobe Acrobat Pro requires a paid subscription and offers extra permission controls; Word can only protect documents it exports itself. BlendPDF is free, works on any existing PDF, and needs no installation or account.

## Remove PDF Metadata

Q: What metadata does a PDF contain?
A: Most PDFs carry hidden fields you never see on the page: the author's name (often a real personal or company account name), title, subject, keywords, the software that created it, and creation and modification timestamps. Many also embed an XMP metadata stream with the same details in XML form.

Q: What exactly does this tool remove?
A: It clears the document information fields (title, author, subject, keywords, creator, producer), deletes the creation and modification dates, and strips the embedded XMP metadata stream. It does not change the visible content of your pages, and it does not remove text, annotations or attachments inside the document.

Q: Is my PDF uploaded to a server?
A: No. Removing metadata runs in your browser, so your file stays on your device. That matters here more than anywhere: you are cleaning a document for privacy, so it should not travel over the internet at all. It only does if you pick an option that needs our server, like converting to Word, and then it's deleted within an hour.

Q: Why should I remove metadata before sharing a PDF?
A: Metadata can quietly reveal who wrote a document, which software and account created it, and exactly when it was made or edited. Removing it before you share a CV, contract, report or public document prevents leaking names, timelines and internal tooling.

Q: Does it work with password-protected PDFs?
A: Not directly — encrypted PDFs can't be modified without the password. Use our Unlock PDF tool to remove the password first, then clean the metadata here.

Q: How can I verify the metadata is really gone?
A: After cleaning, BlendPDF re-opens the cleaned file and reads its metadata back, showing a before/after table where each removed field is confirmed. You can also check the downloaded file yourself in any PDF viewer's document properties.

Q: Does removing metadata change the visible content?
A: No. Pages, text, images, and formatting stay exactly as they were — only the hidden document information fields and the XMP stream are removed. Annotations, attachments, and the text itself are not touched.

Q: What hidden data is NOT removed?
A: The tool removes document-level metadata only. It does not delete annotations, comments, attachments, bookmarks, form data, or sensitive text visible on the pages. If the content itself contains private information, you need to redact it separately.

Q: What is the XMP metadata stream?
A: XMP is an XML block embedded in many PDFs that duplicates and extends the basic metadata — author, software, timestamps, and sometimes document history. Deleting only the info fields leaves XMP behind, which is why this tool strips the whole XMP stream from the document catalog as well.

Q: What are the file size limits?
A: PDF files up to 50MB are supported, with no page limit. Since processing is local, speed depends on your device rather than a server, and metadata removal is fast even for large documents.

Q: Is my original file modified?
A: No. The cleaned PDF is saved as a new file prefixed with "no-metadata-", and your original stays untouched on your device. You keep both versions.

Q: Can I remove metadata on mobile devices?
A: Yes, the tool works on smartphones and tablets. The metadata table, removal button, and download all work in mobile browsers, and processing stays local to your device.

Q: Is removing PDF metadata free?
A: Yes — completely free, with no sign-up, no watermarks, and no premium tiers today. Files up to 50MB are supported, and unlimited documents can be cleaned.

Q: What if metadata removal fails?
A: Common causes are password-protected files (unlock first), corrupted PDFs, or files over 50MB. Some malformed documents can't be re-saved by the cleaning engine. Verify the file opens in a PDF viewer, then try again; if a specific field resists removal, the before/after table will show it honestly.

## Repair PDF Online - Fix Corrupted Files

Q: How does PDF repair work?
A: We use PDF repair algorithms to attempt to fix corruption issues. The tool tries to recover readable pages and data from the corrupted PDF, creating a new repaired version.

Q: What types of corruption can be repaired?
A: We can attempt to repair PDFs with structural corruption, missing or damaged page data, and some formatting issues. Severely corrupted files may not be fully recoverable.

Q: Can you guarantee the PDF will be repaired?
A: While we do our best to repair corrupted PDFs, not all types of corruption can be fixed. The success depends on the extent and type of damage. We'll recover what we can, but some data loss may occur.

Q: Will I lose any data during repair?
A: In some cases, severely corrupted pages may not be recoverable and will be skipped. We'll preserve all pages that can be successfully recovered. The repaired PDF may have fewer pages than the original if some pages were too damaged.

Q: What kinds of PDF damage can be repaired?
A: The tool handles structural damage best: broken cross-reference tables, damaged object references, malformed trailers, files that were not closed properly during saving, and PDFs that some viewers refuse to open even though most of the data is intact. It recovers what is still present in the file — it cannot reconstruct data that is missing.

Q: What kinds of damage cannot be repaired?
A: If the underlying data is gone, no tool can bring it back. Files truncated during download, files whose bytes were overwritten, encrypted files where the encryption data itself is damaged, and files that were never valid PDFs to begin with usually cannot be recovered. Repair restores structure around surviving content; it does not recreate lost content.

Q: Is my PDF guaranteed to be fixed?
A: No, and any tool that promises a 100% success rate is overselling. Success depends on how much of the original data survived. BlendPDF recovers everything it can and returns a rebuilt file, but severely damaged files may come back incomplete or may fail to repair at all.

Q: Will I lose pages or content during repair?
A: Possibly. If individual pages are too damaged to read, the fallback recovery skips them and keeps the rest, so the repaired PDF may have fewer pages than the original. When the primary qpdf repair succeeds, all pages are usually preserved. Always open the repaired file and check it against what you expected.

Q: How do I repair a corrupted PDF online?
A: Upload the damaged PDF (up to 50MB) by dragging it onto the page or clicking Choose File, then click Repair PDF. Processing usually takes a few seconds to a couple of minutes depending on file size. When it finishes, download the repaired copy. No account or email is required.

Q: Is repairing a PDF free? Is there a watermark?
A: Yes, it is completely free. There is no watermark on the output, no page limit, no daily quota that pushes you to a paid plan, and no sign-up. The repaired file is your document, rebuilt — nothing is added to it.

Q: Is it safe to upload a corrupted PDF?
A: Yes. Files travel over an encrypted HTTPS connection and are deleted from our servers within one hour, most immediately after processing. We never read, store, or share the contents of your documents, and no account is needed. We only measure usage as anonymous totals, through Google Analytics and our own count of tool runs, never your documents.

Q: What are the file size limits?
A: One PDF per operation, up to 50MB. Repair is limited to 20 files per 15 minutes per user. Corrupted files sometimes cannot be compressed first, so if your file is over 50MB, try recovering it from its original source instead.

Q: Why do PDFs get corrupted in the first place?
A: Common causes are interrupted downloads or uploads, emailing a file that gets cut off, crashes while an application is saving, failing storage drives or USB sticks, and software that writes non-standard PDF structures. If a file keeps arriving corrupted, re-export it from the source application rather than repairing each copy.

Q: Can you repair a password-protected PDF?
A: Not directly. If the file opens with a password but misbehaves, remove the password first with the Unlock PDF tool, then repair the unlocked copy. If the encryption data itself is corrupted, the file usually cannot be recovered, because the contents are unreadable without intact encryption structures.

Q: Does repair work on scanned PDFs? Do you do OCR?
A: Repair works on scanned PDFs the same way it works on any PDF: it recovers the file structure and the page images inside it. It does not perform OCR, so a scanned PDF stays a set of images and its text will not become selectable or searchable after repair. Run the repaired file through the BlendPDF OCR tool if you need its text to become searchable.

Q: The repaired file still will not open. What now?
A: Try re-downloading or re-exporting the file from its original source, check email or cloud storage for an earlier intact copy, look for previous versions in your backup or file-history tools, or ask the sender to resend it. If several independent tools cannot open the file, the data is most likely gone.

Q: How does this compare to repairing in Adobe Acrobat?
A: Adobe Acrobat quietly rebuilds mildly damaged files when it opens them, but it has no dedicated repair button and requires a paid license for editing features. BlendPDF gives you an explicit repair step, is free, and runs in the browser with nothing to install. For severe corruption, neither approach can recover data that no longer exists in the file.

Q: What should I do if I get an error while repairing?
A: Check that the file is under 50MB and actually a PDF — renaming a .docx to .pdf does not make it one. If you see a "too many requests" message, wait a few minutes; the limit is 20 files per 15 minutes. If a repair fails outright, the file is likely damaged beyond what automated recovery can do.

## Sign PDF Online - Add Electronic Signature

Q: How does PDF signing work?
A: Draw, type, or upload a signature, then drag it exactly where you want it on the page — you can place as many signatures as you need across different pages. The signatures are embedded directly into the PDF, and signing runs in your browser: the file is only uploaded if you pick an option that needs our server, like converting to Word.

Q: How can I create my signature?
A: Three ways: draw it with your mouse or finger, type your name and pick a signature style, or upload an image of your handwritten signature. A PNG with a transparent background looks best, but any common image format works.

Q: Is this a legally binding signature?
A: This tool adds a visual signature to your PDF. For legally binding electronic signatures, you may need specialized services that provide digital certificates and audit trails. This is a simple signature overlay tool.

Q: Can I sign multiple pages?
A: Yes. Use the page navigation to move through the document and place signatures on any pages you like — you can add several signatures and apply them all in one go.

Q: How do I sign a PDF online?
A: Upload your PDF (up to 50MB), then draw, type, or upload a signature and drag it exactly where you want it on the page — you can place several signatures across different pages. Click apply and download the signed copy. Everything runs in your browser and no account is required.

Q: Is this a digital signature or a visual signature?
A: A visual signature. BlendPDF draws your name or signature image onto the page. It is not a cryptographic (PKI) digital signature: there is no certificate, no tamper-evident seal, and PDF viewers will not show a signature-validation panel.

Q: What is the difference between text and image signatures?
A: You can create a signature three ways: draw it with your mouse or finger, type your name in a signature font, or upload an image of your handwritten signature. Typed signatures are fastest; drawn and image signatures look handwritten. A PNG with a transparent background looks best.

Q: How do I make a good signature image?
A: Sign with a dark pen on white paper, photograph or scan it in good light, and crop tightly around the signature. A PNG with a transparent background looks best because the page shows through; a JPEG will carry a white rectangle behind the ink.

Q: Where can I position the signature?
A: Anywhere. The signature appears on a live preview of the page and you drag it to the exact spot you want; a corner handle resizes it. Bottom-right is the classic signature spot, but placement is completely free, so you can land it precisely on a form's signature line.

Q: Can I sign more than one page?
A: Yes, in a single pass. Navigate between pages in the preview, place a signature on every page that needs one, and apply them all at once. Each signature can be positioned and sized independently.

Q: Can I sign in Arabic or other non-Latin scripts?
A: Yes. Type your name in Arabic, Hebrew, Chinese, or any other script and it renders correctly — your browser shapes the text with proper letter joining and right-to-left direction before it is placed on the page. For a handwritten look in any script, an image signature works too.

Q: Is signing PDFs free? Is there a watermark?
A: Yes, completely free, with no watermark, no signature limit, and no trial-then-paywall. No account or email is required; downloads are direct, with an optional email-delivery feature if you want one.

Q: Is it safe to sign documents online?
A: Yes. Signing happens entirely in your browser — your PDF and your signature are never uploaded to a server unless you pick an option that needs our server, like converting to Word, and then the file is deleted within an hour. We only collect aggregate anonymous usage analytics.

Q: Can I sign a password-protected PDF?
A: No, encrypted PDFs cannot be processed. Remove the password first with the Unlock PDF tool (you need the password), sign the unlocked copy, and re-protect it afterward with the Protect PDF tool if needed.

Q: Can I sign a scanned PDF?
A: Yes. The signature is drawn on top of the page, so it works on scanned documents exactly as on digital ones. This is the classic use case: someone emails you a scanned form, you sign it and send it back without printing.

Q: What are the file limits?
A: One PDF up to 50MB per operation. Signature images can be any common format your browser can display — they are converted automatically. There is no page-count limit, and you can place signatures on any pages in the document.

Q: How does this compare to printing and scanning, or Adobe Fill & Sign?
A: Versus print-sign-scan: same visual result, no printer, and the document keeps its quality and selectable text. Versus Adobe Fill & Sign: similar simple e-signature, but BlendPDF runs in the browser with no app or Adobe account. For certificate-based digital signatures, a dedicated service is the right tool.

Q: What should I do if signing fails?
A: Check that the PDF is under 50MB and not password protected — encrypted files must be unlocked first with the Unlock PDF tool. Corrupted files can be run through the Repair PDF tool first, though repair cannot fix everything.
