## Unlock PDF Online - Remove Password

Q: Can I remove PDF restrictions without a password?
A: Yes, if a PDF only has printing, copying, or editing restrictions (owner password), our tool can remove them instantly without requiring you to enter the password.

Q: What's the difference between restrictions and password protection?
A: Restrictions (owner password) prevent you from printing, copying text, or editing the document, but still allow you to open it. Password protection (user/open password) encrypts the entire file and prevents you from even opening it without the password.

Q: Is it legal to remove PDF restrictions?
A: Yes, it is legal to remove restrictions from PDFs that you own, created, or have the legal right to modify. Do not use this tool on copyrighted materials you do not have rights to.

Q: What restrictions can be removed?
A: Our tool removes printing locks, text/image copying restrictions, document assembly locks, and form filling restrictions.

Q: How does PDF unlocking work?
A: We use the password you provide to decrypt the PDF. The password is required to unlock the file. Once unlocked, the PDF can be opened without a password.

Q: What if I forgot the password?
A: Unfortunately, if you don't know the password, we cannot unlock the PDF. The encryption is designed to be secure, so the password is required. Make sure you have the correct password before attempting to unlock.

Q: Is it safe to unlock PDFs here?
A: Yes. Your files are processed securely and never stored — Files are deleted from our servers within 1 hour — most immediately after processing. We never keep your PDFs or passwords.

Q: What if my PDF is not password-protected?
A: If your PDF is not encrypted, you don't need to unlock it. Simply open it normally. This tool is only for PDFs that require a password to open.

Q: How do I unlock a PDF online?
A: Upload the PDF and choose a mode. "Remove Restrictions" strips printing, copying, and editing locks without a password. "Unlock with Password" removes an open password, but you must enter the correct password. Download the unlocked copy when processing finishes.

Q: Can BlendPDF recover or crack a forgotten PDF password?
A: No. If a PDF requires a password to open and you do not know it, BlendPDF cannot unlock it. Modern PDF encryption is designed so the password is mathematically required. No honest online tool can bypass it.

Q: Is it legal to unlock a PDF?
A: It is generally lawful to unlock documents you own, created, or have the right to modify, such as your own files or documents shared with you for editing. Do not use it to bypass protection on copyrighted material or documents you have no rights to; laws vary by country.

Q: Is it safe to unlock a PDF online?
A: Yes. Files and passwords travel over encrypted HTTPS, the password is used once for decryption and never stored, and files are deleted from our servers within one hour, most immediately after processing. Document contents are never read, stored, or shared; we only collect aggregate anonymous usage analytics.

Q: Is unlocking PDFs free, and do I need an account?
A: Yes, it is completely free with no watermark and no hidden paywall, and no account or email is required. An optional email-delivery feature exists, but direct download never asks for an email.

Q: Which encryption types are supported?
A: BlendPDF handles standard PDF encryption as defined in the PDF specification, from older 40-bit and 128-bit RC4 files up to modern AES-128 and AES-256. Non-standard DRM systems (like Adobe LiveCycle rights management) are not supported.

Q: What are the file size limits?
A: One PDF per operation, up to 50MB. Larger files should be compressed first, though a password-protected file must be unlocked before other tools can process it.

Q: Will unlocking change my document?
A: No. Unlocking decrypts the file and removes the security settings; the pages themselves are not re-rendered. Text, images, fonts, layout, links, and form fields are unchanged, and your original file on your device is untouched.

Q: Why does it say my password is incorrect?
A: Passwords are case-sensitive and must match exactly, including spaces and special characters. Check for Caps Lock, keyboard layout differences, and copy-paste that includes a trailing space. If the correct password truly fails, the file may use non-standard protection.

Q: Why does it say the PDF already has no restrictions?
A: The file is not encrypted and has no permission locks, so there is nothing to remove. If an app still blocks copying or printing, the limitation comes from the app or from the PDF being a scanned image, not from PDF security.

Q: Why do I need to unlock a PDF before using other tools?
A: Encrypted PDFs cannot be read by processing tools, so merge, compress, sign, and conversion tools fail on them. Unlock the file first, run the tool you need, then re-protect the result with the Protect PDF tool if you want a password back on it.

Q: How does BlendPDF compare to Adobe Acrobat or print-to-PDF workarounds?
A: Acrobat Pro can remove security but requires a paid subscription and the password. Printing to a new PDF sometimes bypasses restrictions but destroys text quality, links, and structure. BlendPDF removes security properly, keeps the document intact, and is free.

## Add Watermark to PDF Online

Q: How does watermarking work?
A: We embed the watermark directly into your PDF. Text watermarks are added as text overlays, while image watermarks are embedded as images. The watermark becomes part of the PDF file.

Q: What's the difference between text and image watermarks?
A: Text watermarks are simple text overlays (like 'DRAFT' or 'CONFIDENTIAL'). Image watermarks use an image file (PNG or JPEG) that you upload. Both can be positioned and adjusted for opacity.

Q: What position options are available?
A: You can place watermarks in the center, diagonally across the page, or in a tiled pattern that repeats across the entire document.

Q: Can I remove a watermark later?
A: Once a watermark is embedded in a PDF, it becomes part of the file. To remove it, you would need to use a PDF editor or recreate the PDF without the watermark.

Q: How does adding a watermark to a PDF work?
A: BlendPDF draws your watermark directly into the content of every page. Text watermarks are rendered in bold gray type at the size and opacity you choose; image watermarks embed a PNG or JPEG you upload. The watermark becomes part of the PDF itself, so it shows up in every viewer and in print.

Q: How do I add a watermark to a PDF online?
A: Upload your PDF (up to 50MB), choose text or image mode, type the text or upload a PNG/JPEG, pick a position (center, diagonal, or tiled), adjust opacity and size while watching the live preview, then click to apply and download the watermarked copy. No account or email is required.

Q: Is the watermark tool free? Does BlendPDF add its own branding?
A: Yes, it is completely free, and no, BlendPDF never adds its own watermark or branding. The only watermark on the output is the one you chose. There are no page limits, daily quotas, or premium tiers.

Q: What watermark positions are available?
A: Three: center (horizontal, middle of the page), diagonal (rotated 45 degrees across the middle — the classic DRAFT look), and tiled (repeated in a grid across the whole page, which is the hardest to crop out). The same position is applied to every page.

Q: Can I control the opacity and size of the watermark?
A: Yes. Opacity runs from 10% to 100% (30% is the default and works well for labels that should not obscure content). Text size is adjustable from 12 to 120 points. A live preview shows the effect on your actual first page before you commit.

Q: Can I use Arabic or other non-Latin text in a watermark?
A: Yes. Type Arabic, Hebrew, Chinese, or any other script directly into the text field and it just works — the watermark is shaped and rendered right in your browser, with correct Arabic letter joining and right-to-left direction, then stamped onto every page. No workaround needed.

Q: Does the watermark appear on every page?
A: Yes, the watermark is applied to all pages of the document. There is currently no option to watermark only a page range. If you need that, split the PDF first, watermark the part that needs it, and merge the parts back together with our Split and Merge tools.

Q: Can a watermark be removed later? Does it protect my document?
A: Be realistic: a watermark deters casual misuse but is not security. It becomes part of the page content and cannot be removed in a viewer, but someone with a PDF editor and time can remove it — especially a single centered mark. Tiled watermarks at moderate opacity are harder to clean. For actual protection, use the Protect PDF tool, which encrypts the file with AES-256.

Q: Is it safe to watermark confidential documents online?
A: Yes. Files travel over an encrypted HTTPS connection and are deleted from our servers within one hour, most immediately after processing. We never read, store, or share document contents, and no account is needed. We only measure usage as anonymous totals, through Google Analytics and our own count of tool runs, never your documents.

Q: Can I watermark a password-protected PDF?
A: No — remove the password first using the Unlock PDF tool (you need to know the password), apply the watermark, then re-protect the file with the Protect PDF tool if you want it encrypted again.

Q: Does watermarking work on scanned PDFs?
A: Yes, and it works well. The watermark is drawn on top of each page, and a scanned page is just an image, so the mark sits over the scan exactly as it would over regular text. No OCR is involved or needed for watermarking. If you also want the scanned text to become searchable, run the file through the BlendPDF OCR tool before or after watermarking.

Q: What are the file size limits?
A: One PDF per operation, up to 50MB, and up to 20 files per 15 minutes per user. Watermark images must be PNG or JPEG. If your PDF is over 50MB, run it through the Compress PDF tool first.

Q: How does this compare to watermarking in Word or Adobe Acrobat?
A: Word can only watermark documents it can open and edit, and re-exporting a PDF through Word often changes the layout. Acrobat Pro has powerful watermark options but requires a paid subscription. BlendPDF works on any existing PDF without touching its layout, is free, and needs no installation or account.

Q: What should I do if I get an error while watermarking?
A: The most common errors: a watermark image that is not PNG/JPEG, a file over 50MB, or a "too many requests" message (wait a few minutes; the limit is 20 files per 15 minutes). If a valid file still fails, it may be corrupted — try the Repair PDF tool first.

Q: What Word formats are supported?
A: We support Microsoft Word (.doc, .docx), OpenDocument Text (.odt), and Rich Text Format (.rtf) files. All formats will be converted to high-quality PDFs.

Q: Will the layout stay the same?

Q: What are the file size limits?
A: You can convert Word documents up to 50MB in size. There's no limit on the number of pages, but larger files may take longer to process.

Q: Is my document secure?

A: Upload your Word document by clicking the select button or dragging it onto the upload area, click "Convert to PDF", and download the result. Conversion takes seconds for typical documents. No account or email is required, and there is no watermark.

Q: Which file formats are supported?
A: Microsoft Word .doc and .docx, OpenDocument .odt, and Rich Text Format .rtf. All of them convert to a standard PDF that opens anywhere. Files can be up to 50MB.

Q: Is the Word to PDF converter really free?
A: Yes. No watermark on the PDF, no page limits, no conversion quota that pushes you to a paid plan, and no sign-up. The technical limits are 50MB per file and about 10 conversions per 15 minutes.

Q: Is it safe to upload my document?
A: Files are uploaded over an encrypted connection, document contents are never read, stored, or shared, and files are deleted from our servers within one hour, most immediately after processing. No account is needed. We only measure usage as anonymous totals, through Google Analytics and our own count of tool runs, never your documents.

Q: Why does my PDF look slightly different from the Word file?
A: Almost always fonts. If your document uses a font that is not available on the conversion server, a similar font is substituted, which can shift line breaks and page breaks. Using widely available fonts, or checking the PDF before sharing it, avoids surprises.

Q: Are hyperlinks, tables of contents, and page numbers kept?
A: Yes for the common cases: hyperlinks remain clickable, page numbers and headers and footers are rendered, and a generated table of contents converts as it appeared when the file was last saved. Dynamic fields are rendered at their last-updated values.

Q: Does it work with Arabic Word documents?
A: Yes. The LibreOffice engine has mature right-to-left support, so Arabic text direction, alignment, and letter joining convert correctly. The main caveat is fonts: if your Arabic font is not available on the server, a substitute is used, which can slightly change the look.

Q: Can I convert a password-protected Word document?
A: No. A password-protected Word file cannot be opened by the converter. Remove the password in Word first (File > Info > Protect Document), convert it here, and then, if you want protection back, use the BlendPDF protect tool to encrypt the PDF with AES-256.

Q: How do I password-protect the PDF I create?
A: Convert your document first, then run the result through the BlendPDF protect tool, which applies real AES-256 encryption with a password you choose. Together the two tools take under a minute.

Q: Can I edit the PDF afterward, or convert it back to Word?
A: Yes. Edit PDF lets you add text in Arabic or English, images, signatures and highlights, and fix the pages, and its Edit text tool (beta) can change a line that's already there, all right in your browser. For bigger changes to the wording, edit your original Word file and convert it again, or turn the PDF back into a DOCX with PDF to Word.

Q: Why use this instead of Word's built-in Save as PDF?
A: If you have desktop Word, its built-in PDF export is excellent and you should feel free to use it. BlendPDF is for everyone else: no Word license, working on a phone or a locked-down computer, converting .odt or .rtf files, or needing a quick conversion without opening an editor.

Q: What should I check before and after converting?
A: Before: accept or reject tracked changes and delete stray comments, since the PDF renders the document as it would print. After: skim the PDF for font substitutions or shifted page breaks. If something fails, check the file opens in a word processor and is under 50MB.
